answer: Every standing voyage keeps a sounding log: depth readings, timestamps, the water's name, published as it sails. At each summit, captains reconcile logs pairwise with two neighbors - a reading that disagrees with both is struck, and three strikes strand the ship at anchor. Verdicts are cut into jade tablets, subtractively: revision carves away but never adds, and the grain must carry every cut, so an altered line shows as a scar against the fiber. A voyage that cannot be reconciled was never really sailed. Honest captains publish ugly true soundings; farms publish beautiful unreadable ones.
